title: The NI cut relies on exactly matching levy receipts
label: Costing uncertainty
text: The table pairs £7.14bn of migrant-levy receipts with £7.14bn of employer NI cuts in 2028/29, with matching figures in every later year. Yet the levy is meant to encourage substitution and automation that can shrink its own tax base.

links.label: Examine the levy and its funding

title: The arithmetic is published; the model is not
label: Costing uncertainty
text: Reform calls the plan fully costed and publishes its totals. The plan and linked policy page do not supply the model needed to reproduce them. Our audit tests all 20 policy lines reaching £1bn in any forecast year against six disclosure questions.

title: Overtime’s behavioural cost needs an explanation
label: Costing uncertainty
text: Tax Policy Associates’ May estimate was about £14bn, including roughly £7bn of pay relabelling and £3bn of company arbitrage. Reform’s October table shows £4.44–£8.54bn from 2028/29 to 2031/32. Different vintages and assumptions make these non-like-for-like figures, not a directly measurable extra shortfall.

title: Keeping settled status does not settle benefit rights
label: Legal obstacle
text: Reform’s FAQ keeps settled status but removes welfare. Current EUSS guidance and UK-law deeming protect benefit rights, while the Withdrawal Agreement protects equal treatment for people within its scope. Those distinct protections need a specific compatibility assessment.

title: EU carbon-border rules already operate
label: Distributional trade-off
text: The EU’s definitive CBAM began in January 2026 and allows credit for verified carbon charges paid abroad. Abolishing the UK ETS could increase the EU importer’s charge on covered British exports while reducing domestic carbon costs. Linkage and exemptions remain contingent on agreement.

title: A £486 tax cut can leave about £219 after UC
label: Distributional trade-off
text: If the whole income-tax gain is exposed to the 55% Universal Credit earnings taper and enough entitlement remains, UC falls £267.30 and the household keeps £218.70. This conditional example excludes council-tax support and other interactions.

title: Energy policy costs are real; so is gas exposure
label: Distributional trade-off
text: IFS puts taxes and levies excluding VAT at about 17% of the average household electricity bill in July–October 2026. That is not the combined energy bill. Gas-driven wholesale pricing remains a separate cause, and moving costs to taxation does not eliminate them.

title: There are credible diagnoses and worthwhile aims
label: Reasonable policy with caveats
text: The OBR documents firms bunching below the VAT registration threshold. Addressing that barrier has merit, as does improving nuclear regulation. The remaining questions concern the remedy, cost, safety and delivery—not whether every diagnosis is false.
